result.title: PruneNAS: Constraint Aware Neural Architecture Search based Pruning
result.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures, British Machine Vision Conference, Lancaster, 2026
result.summary: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has achieved state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks, but its high computational cost remains a major barrier. We introduce PruneNAS, a novel framework that integrates structured pruning into NAS to efficiently explore high-performing architectures while leveraging pretrained models. Unlike conventional NAS methods that train each candidate from scratch, PruneNAS generates a candidate pool by pruning pretrained networks at multiple granularity levels and formulates the selection as a global optimization problem using training-free importance metrics. This approach enables rapid evaluation of candidate architectures under strict resource constraints, dramatically reducing search time from hundreds of GPU hours to mere minutes. Experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that PruneNAS discovers compact, high-accuracy architectures that nearly halve the computational cost (MACs) of prior methods on ResNet-50, while also showing strong generalization on object detection tasks with YOLO. Our method bridges structured pruning and NAS, offering a practical solution for resource-constrained model deployment.

AI.brief_summary: PruneNAS 将结构化剪枝与 NAS 结合，通过在多粒度层级剪枝预训练网络生成候选池，并用免训练重要性指标做全局优化选择，从而在资源约束下快速得到紧凑高精度架构。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作面向 CNN 架构搜索与部署效率（ResNet-50、YOLO），不涉及多模态推理、latent 状态生成或证据筛选，免训练重要性指标用于权重与层选择而非推理期内部表示，缺少可核查的具体借鉴线索。
